bounded_claims_supported: Accuracy, integrity, completeness and timeliness are distinct aggregation principles.
Risk data should be reconciled to sources; a ledger is not automatically its own control.
claims_not_supported: BCBS 239 defines a row-matching algorithm or materiality numeric.
limitations: Supervisory principles for banks; not a software contract.
source_authority_scope: Risk-data aggregation principles including reconciliation to sources
title: Principles for effective risk data aggregation and risk reporting

bounded_claims_supported: ADWIN provides an adaptive-window change detector with stated statistical guarantees.
claims_not_supported: A detected change point is a quality defect verdict.
limitations: Detector method, not adjudication.
title: Learning from Time-Changing Data with Adaptive Windowing

bounded_claims_supported: SIP, AIP and DIP are distinct information packages.
PDI includes Reference, Context, Provenance, Fixity and Access Rights Information.
An OAIS has accepted long-term preservation responsibility for a designated community.
claims_not_supported: OAIS is forensic chain-of-custody or legal retention authority.
limitations: Reference model, not a byte-level package format. Full ISO text is paywalled; CCSDS magenta book is the adopted technical content.
source_authority_scope: Long-term digital preservation information packages and PDI
title: Reference Model for an Open Archival Information System (OAIS)

bounded_claims_supported: Binds payload type into the signature; envelope verification is not predicate truth.
claims_not_supported: Verified envelope implies issuer authority for the claim.
limitations: Envelope format only.
title: Dead Simple Signing Envelope

bounded_claims_supported: Data subjects hold rights of access, rectification and erasure subject to conditions.
Erasure obligations interact with other EU/national law, including retention duties.
claims_not_supported: GDPR defines technical deletion APIs or retention TTLs.
limitations: Text not independently archived in this run beyond EUR-Lex access; legal interpretation is out of research scope.
source_authority_scope: One erasure-authority regime conflicting with technical retention authorities
title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)

bounded_claims_supported: Findability, accessibility, interoperability and reuse are stewardship principles.
claims_not_supported: FAIR scores prove scientific reproducibility of a run.
limitations: Principles, not a package format (see RO-Crate).
title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship

bounded_claims_supported: ALCOA: attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original or true copy, accurate.
Amendments retain history; they are not silent overwrite.
claims_not_supported: FDA CGMP is a universal data-platform mutation API.
limitations: Drug CGMP scope; other jurisdictions differ.
source_authority_scope: Record integrity expectations for FDA-regulated drug CGMP records
title: Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP: Questions and Answers

bounded_claims_supported: MMD tests whether two samples are from the same distribution under stated assumptions.
claims_not_supported: A significant MMD is a business defect or authorized correction.
limitations: Statistical method paper; not a quality judgment authority.
title: A Kernel Two-Sample Test

bounded_claims_supported: An Evidence Record preserves long-term non-repudiation via hash trees and archive timestamps.
Renewal addresses hash-algorithm weakening; it does not restate claim truth.
claims_not_supported: ERS is PREMIS preservation metadata or chain-of-custody law.
limitations: Cryptographic long-term validation, not archival information packages.
source_authority_scope: Long-term cryptographic evidence records and archive timestamps
title: RFC 4998: Evidence Record Syntax (ERS)

bounded_claims_supported: Structured syslog transport carries logged events between originator, relay and collector.
claims_not_supported: Delivery implies completeness, durability or evidentiary admissibility.
limitations: Transport protocol; filtering and loss are expected operationally.
title: The Syslog Protocol

bounded_claims_supported: JCS defines a deterministic JSON serialization for comparable hashes.
Canonical JSON equality is not semantic or RDF dataset equality.
claims_not_supported: Canonical bytes prove claim truth or issuer authority.
limitations: Does not canonicalize numbers beyond IEEE-754 concerns documented in the RFC; not RDF-aware.
title: RFC 8785: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)

bounded_claims_supported: Merkle inclusion and consistency proofs for append-only logs.
claims_not_supported: Log inclusion is certificate trustworthiness or quality certification.
limitations: CT-specific; SCITT generalizes supply-chain statements.
title: RFC 9162: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0

bounded_claims_supported: Attester, Verifier and Relying Party are distinct roles.
Evidence, Endorsements, Reference Values, Appraisal Policy, Attestation Results and relying-party authorization are distinct messages.
Appraisal of Evidence is not the relying-party application decision.
claims_not_supported: Attestation Results are claim truth.
RATS is a general data-quality appraisal calculus.
limitations: Architecture and terminology, not a wire format. EAT/COSE profiles are separate RFCs.
source_authority_scope: Remote attestation roles and conceptual messages
title: RFC 9334: Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Architecture

bounded_claims_supported: Receipts prove properties of a verifiable data structure to a verifier.
Transparency services issue receipts per RFC 9943 registration flows.
claims_not_supported: A receipt states or appraises registered-statement truth.
limitations: COSE encoding layer of the SCITT architecture only.
source_authority_scope: Receipt proof format over verifiable data structures
title: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts

bounded_claims_supported: Issuer Signed Statement, Transparency Service registration, Receipt and Relying Party verification are distinct.
A receipt is a proof about a verifiable data structure, not statement truth.
claims_not_supported: Registration implies claim correctness or quality certification.
limitations: Architecture; COSE Receipts are RFC 9942.
title: RFC 9943: An Architecture for Trustworthy and Transparent Digital Supply Chains (SCITT)

bounded_claims_supported: Accounting policies, accounting estimates and prior-period errors are distinct.
Material is defined by reference to IAS 1; IAS 8 does not supply a numeric materiality threshold or a row-match tolerance.
Policy changes and error corrections are generally retrospective; estimate changes are prospective.
claims_not_supported: Materiality is a data-quality metric.
A reconciliation break residual is an IAS 8 error by default.
limitations: Financial-statement scope; settlement/finality of payments is outside IAS 8.
source_authority_scope: Policy versus estimate versus error, and materiality-by-reference, not match tolerance
title: IAS 8 Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors

bounded_claims_supported: A Statement binds immutable digest-identified subjects to a typed predicate.
Subject matching is by digest, not filename semantics.
The Statement is not the signature envelope and not an appraisal result.
claims_not_supported: A typed attestation predicate is true or independently appraised.
limitations: Does not define Verifier appraisal policy; DSSE/COSE envelopes are separate.
title: in-toto Attestation Framework Statement layer v1

bounded_claims_supported: Defines a general data-quality model with inherent and system-dependent characteristics.
Characteristics are independently named; the standard is for requirements, measures and evaluations.
claims_not_supported: Public landing page republishes the full characteristic definitions.
limitations: Full text paywalled; characteristic split used here is corroborated by ISO 25000 overview and peer-reviewed application papers, not a substitute for the standard text.
source_authority_scope: Existence and scope of the SQuaRE data-quality model
title: ISO/IEC 25012:2008 Software engineering — SQuaRE — Data quality model

bounded_claims_supported: Addresses identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of digital evidence.
claims_not_supported: Landing page is the full acquisition procedure or legal admissibility test.
limitations: Full text paywalled.
title: ISO/IEC 27037:2012 Guidelines for identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of digital evidence

bounded_claims_supported: Defines acceptance sampling plans indexed by AQL.
claims_not_supported: A sample statistic is a population claim without the plan and frame.
limitations: Full text paywalled; AQL lot disposition is not a fitness-for-use policy.
title: ISO 2859-1:1999 Sampling procedures for inspection by attributes

bounded_claims_supported: Measurement, measurand, measurement result, error and uncertainty are distinct terms.
claims_not_supported: VIM defines data-quality dimensions or fitness-for-use policies.
limitations: Metrology vocabulary, not data-governance policy.
title: JCGM 200:2012 International vocabulary of metrology (VIM)

bounded_claims_supported: Collection, examination, analysis and reporting are distinct forensic stages.
claims_not_supported: Guidance is legal admissibility in a named court.
limitations: US federal guidance; dated relative to later NISTIR evidence-handler notes.
title: NIST SP 800-86 Guide to Integrating Forensic Techniques into Incident Response

bounded_claims_supported: Defines approved hash algorithms and digest computation.
claims_not_supported: A digest is identity, authenticity, or truth.
limitations: Integrity primitive only.
title: FIPS 180-4 Secure Hash Standard

bounded_claims_supported: Advisory documents carry tracking status draft/interim/final with revision history, enabling supersession.
Product status enumerations (first_affected, last_affected, known_affected, known_not_affected, fixed, recommended, under_investigation) do not include a recall state.
claims_not_supported: CSAF is a data-quality or provenance interchange.
A superseding advisory rewrites or erases prior editions.
limitations: Security-advisory scope only; used solely to bound supersession vocabulary.
source_authority_scope: Advisory document lifecycle and product-status vocabulary
title: Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) Version 2.0

bounded_claims_supported: Defines a document structure spanning schema, quality, SLA, roles and servers.
claims_not_supported: ODCS is the unique semantic owner of declared contracts.
limitations: Competes with other contract documents; not ISO.
title: Open Data Contract Standard 3.1.0

bounded_claims_supported: Case files, stages, sentries and discretionary work model case lifecycle.
claims_not_supported: Opening a case is a defect verdict or a correction authorization.
limitations: Case notation, not quality policy.
title: Case Management Model and Notation 1.1

bounded_claims_supported: Assurance cases separate claims, structured arguments and evidence references.
An argument is an asserted position, not an automatic adjudication.
claims_not_supported: SACM is a RATS appraisal procedure or a data-quality metric algebra.
limitations: Metamodel; method quality and legal admissibility are out of scope.
title: Structured Assurance Case Metamodel (SACM) 2.3

bounded_claims_supported: success records whether issues were found; severity records configured enforcement consequence.
Dataset-attached assertions are not the same as run-level TestRunFacet records.
claims_not_supported: A failed advisory assertion is a defect verdict or authorized mutation.
limitations: Interchange facet only; no adjudication, waiver or correction semantics.
source_authority_scope: Assertion observation attached to a dataset in an OpenLineage event
title: OpenLineage Data Quality Assertions Facet

bounded_claims_supported: RunEvent is runtime observation; JobEvent and DatasetEvent are design-time metadata and are not associated with a Run.
Job, Run and Dataset are distinct identities; facets extend them without becoming identity.
DataQualityAssertionsDatasetFacet separates assertion success from configured severity.
claims_not_supported: OpenLineage is the canonical semantic owner of lineage.
A RunEvent proves derivation, causation or PROV validity.
Quality facets are publication authority or fitness verdicts.
limitations: Project specification, not an international standard. Facet set is extensible and version-bound.
source_authority_scope: OpenLineage event kinds, job/run/dataset identities and documented facets
title: OpenLineage Object Model 1.52.0

bounded_claims_supported: A dataset may be referenced by a physical location in one context and a logical name in another.
The symlinks facet lists alternative identifiers; it does not prove the identifiers denote one SAN identity.
claims_not_supported: Symlink equality is approved master-data identity or PROV alternateOf.
limitations: Encoding facet; OpenLineage is not the SAN identity owner.
source_authority_scope: Physical versus logical dataset identifiers in OpenLineage events
title: OpenLineage Symlinks Dataset Facet

bounded_claims_supported: Defines a log-record model with trace correlation fields.
claims_not_supported: Telemetry is durable evidence, provenance, or quality adjudication.
limitations: Observability interchange, not evidence qualification.
title: OpenTelemetry Logs Data Model

authors_or_issuer: Library of Congress PREMIS Editorial Committee
bounded_claims_supported: Objects, Events, Agents and Rights are distinct preservation-metadata entities.
Events document actions on objects; they are not PROV validity and not legal admissibility.
claims_not_supported: PREMIS Rights are access-control enforcement or GDPR erasure authority.
limitations: Minimum semantic units; implementers combine other technical metadata. Canonical PDF blocks automated retrieval; claims rest on the official v3 site.
source_authority_scope: Preservation metadata entities and semantic units
title: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata 3.0

bounded_claims_supported: Packages research objects with contextual metadata and a manifest.
claims_not_supported: A valid crate is a successful reproduction or scientific truth.
limitations: Superseded by RO-Crate 1.2.0 (June 2025) and 1.3 for new work; packaging only, not evaluation.
title: RO-Crate Metadata Specification 1.1

bounded_claims_supported: Separates scalable analyzers, constraint suggestion and constraint verification.
claims_not_supported: Suggested constraints are authorized requirements.
limitations: Implementation evidence in Deequ is not a semantic owner.
source_authority_scope: Profiling versus verification method split at scale
title: Automating Large-Scale Data Quality Verification

bounded_claims_supported: Broker-dealer record preservation periods and WORM/audit-trail expectations in that regime.
claims_not_supported: SEC retention is a universal technical TTL or GDPR erasure rule.
limitations: US broker-dealer scope; conflicts with other retention authorities are expected.
title: 17 CFR 240.17a-4 Records to be preserved by certain exchange members

bounded_claims_supported: DID documents expose verification methods and service endpoints.
claims_not_supported: Resolving a verification method appraises a claim or establishes trust policy.
limitations: Resolution is effectful and method-specific.
title: Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0

bounded_claims_supported: Dimension, Metric, QualityMeasurement, QualityAnnotation, QualityPolicy and QualityCertificate are distinct classes.
A metric is a procedure for measuring a dimension; a measurement assigns a value to a metric.
Fitness judgments are left to consumers rather than implied by a metric value.
claims_not_supported: A universal numeric quality score exists.
A quality certificate proves dataset fitness for every use.
limitations: Working Group Note, not a W3C Recommendation. Does not specify reconciliation, sampling or mutation authority.
source_authority_scope: Quality metadata vocabulary separating dimension, metric, measurement, annotation, policy and certificate
title: Data on the Web Best Practices: Data Quality Vocabulary

bounded_claims_supported: Describes discovery and retrieval of provenance descriptions.
claims_not_supported: Query results confirm impact or closed-world completeness.
limitations: Note, not a query algebra standard such as SPARQL.
title: PROV-AQ: Provenance Access and Query

bounded_claims_supported: Validity is defined via uniqueness, event-ordering, impossibility and type constraints plus normalization.
Equivalence is comparison of normal forms, not surface syntax.
Validation is implementation-independent if the same instances are accepted or rejected.
claims_not_supported: A valid PROV instance is historically true.
Validation completeness implies closed-world absence of unrecorded edges.
limitations: Polynomial-time reference procedure; terminating chase depends on weak acyclicity of the specified dependencies.
source_authority_scope: PROV instance validity, equivalence and constraint checking
title: Constraints of the PROV Data Model

bounded_claims_supported: Entities, activities and agents are the core PROV types.
wasDerivedFrom is a derivation relation, not a causal law.
A bundle is a named set of provenance descriptions and may itself be an entity.
An entity description has fixed aspects for its lifetime; material change requires a new entity.
claims_not_supported: Provenance statements are true.
Derivation implies causation or correctness.
Bundle membership is issuer endorsement or evidence sufficiency.
limitations: Does not define runtime job/run/dataset lineage or cryptographic attestation.
source_authority_scope: PROV data-model types, relations, bundles and derivation for interchange of provenance descriptions
title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model

bounded_claims_supported: Entity, Activity and Agent are distinct classes.
A Bundle is a named set of provenance descriptions that may itself have provenance; adding or removing a triple creates a distinct bundle.
Invalidation is cessation of an entity and is distinct from generation and usage.
claims_not_supported: PROV-O defines redaction, disclosure policy or cryptographic evidence decay.
Influence is a causal law.
limitations: OWL encoding of PROV-DM; does not add a SAN disclosure algebra.
source_authority_scope: RDF/OWL encoding of PROV types including Bundle and invalidation
title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology

bounded_claims_supported: Defines a canonical N-Quads form for RDF datasets for comparison and securing.
Implementations must bound work; poison graphs can be adversarial.
claims_not_supported: RDF canonical equality is JSON JCS equality or PROV semantic equivalence.
limitations: Computationally sensitive; not a provenance algebra.
title: RDF Dataset Canonicalization

bounded_claims_supported: SHACL defines shapes, constraint components and validation reports for RDF graphs.
claims_not_supported: Conformance is fitness, publication eligibility or gate disposition.
limitations: RDF-focused; other schema languages are not SHACL.
title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)

bounded_claims_supported: Assertions, variables, filters and consistency checks over XBRL facts.
claims_not_supported: XBRL Formula is a general SQL quality DSL.
limitations: XBRL fact-model specific. OIM-compatible Formula is only a Candidate Recommendation (CR 2024-02-14), not a Recommendation.
title: XBRL Formula 1.0
